title: Conserved mRNP remodeling mechanism of the TREX-2.1 complex

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and unzipped the Europe PMC supplementary package (5.78 MB) and read all 11 pages of gkag884_supplemental_file.pdf: Tables S1-S7 are reagent lists, 9 plasmids, 4 oligos, ~11 yeast strains, and the crosslink tables. I counted the crosslink rows by hand: Table S5 has 7 rows (6 to Csn12, 1 to Thp3) and Table S6 has 4 rows, so 11 measured crosslinks total, printed as PDF text with no machine-readable file. I pulled the RCSB (Protein Data Bank) metadata record for entry 9ZEB: one cryo-EM (cryogenic electron microscopy) structure, 4 protein chains, 3.72 Angstrom resolution, 57,575 particles. The EMDB (Electron Microscopy Data Bank) entry EMD-74098 responds with HTTP 200 and is public.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The ATPase (enzyme that hydrolyses ATP) assay results, the TIRF (total internal reflection fluorescence) microscopy co-localization percentages and the yeast growth/qPCR phenotypes exist only as figure panels; I did not find them as numeric tables. The PRIDE (PRoteomics IDEntifications) deposit PXD073414 returned HTTP 404 from both the v2 and v3 Application Programming Interface endpoints, so I could not confirm it is released or see its file list.

a1_downloadable.note: Structure data is public and needs no login: PDB entry 9ZEB and EMDB map EMD-74098 both resolve, and the supplement PDF downloaded. Caveat verified by me: the mass spectrometry deposit PXD073414 is not yet retrievable (404 from PRIDE).

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAILS. There is no prediction target column anywhere in these files. Any label a model could learn (for example, whether a residue pair crosslinks, or whether a mutation abolishes binding) would have to be constructed by reading values out of figure panels and a PDF table by hand.

a3_inputs_present.note: Not the blocker. Protein sequences for the four chains (Thp3, Csn12, Sem1, Sub2) are inside the PDB entry, so inputs would be present if a label existed.

a4_units_stated.note: Units are stated where numbers exist: spectral counts for crosslinks, Angstroms for resolution. But these are summary statistics of one experiment, not a measurement column.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAILS, verified by counting rows in the PDF. 11 crosslinked peptide pairs across two tables, plus one structure of one four-protein complex. The checklist bar is ~1,500 labelled rows (or ~400 for classification); this is two to three orders of magnitude short.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~6 MB supplement + ~30 MB cryo-EM map; trivially small
a6_fits_laptop.note: Not the blocker. Everything fits in memory many times over.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: The numbers agree: the paper and Supplementary Figure S3 say 57,575 particles at 3.72 Angstrom, and the RCSB metadata record for 9ZEB reports exactly 57,575 particles at 3.72 Angstrom.

a8_label_provenance.note: Moot, because there is no label. The crosslinks that do exist are genuine measurements (pLink3 software, 5% false discovery rate cutoff), not another model's output, so provenance is not the problem here.

backbone.name: ESM-2 (a protein language model) or AlphaFold-Multimer (a structure predictor), either of which could in principle embed these four protein sequences
backbone.hardware: CPU is ample for 4 sequences, but there is nothing to fit a head to
backbone.licence: ESM-2 weights are MIT-licensed; PDB and EMDB data are public domain (CC0)

integration.partner_dataset: None usable. In principle the four chains carry UniProt accessions that join to AlphaFold DB or the wider PDB, but joining 4 proteins to anything adds 4 rows.
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Cannot be written: with one complex and eleven crosslinks there is no question a join could answer that the structure paper has not already answered directly.

controls.positive_control: None available at this scale; the eleven crosslinks are themselves the paper's validation of the structure, so there is nothing left to hold out.
controls.negative_control: Label shuffling is not meaningful on 11 rows.
controls.external_validation: Related structures exist (PDB 7EWM for apo scTREX-2.1, 5SUP for Sub2-Yra1-RNA, 8ENK for DDX39B-Tho1-RNA), but these are a handful of structures, not a validation set.

honest_claim_h3: No honest machine-learning claim is possible from this paper's data: with one 3.72 Angstrom structure, eleven crosslinked peptide pairs and no outcome column, any model would be fitting noise.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use protein sequence and structure to predict which residue pairs crosslink when two mRNA-export proteins touch.
plain_idea.train_on: The project I considered would show a model each pair of nearby residues across the four proteins in the complex (Thp3, Csn12, Sem1, Sub2), with their sequence neighbourhoods and structural context. The paper supplies 11 verified crosslink observations, a number I counted in the supplementary PDF.
plain_idea.predict: Whether a given residue pair is captured as a crosslink, with the true answer coming from photo-crosslinking mass spectrometry: an unnatural amino acid (pBpa) placed at three chosen positions in Sub2, activated with ultraviolet light, and the resulting joined peptides identified by pLink3 software at a 5% false discovery rate.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Structural biologists would like to predict crosslink sites before running the experiment, but this paper provides 11 examples from three probe positions in one complex, which cannot train or test anything. It is a fine mechanism paper and not a dataset.

ml_idea: None viable. The data is one cryo-EM structure of the four-protein TREX-2.1 complex bound to the helicase Sub2 (PDB 9ZEB, EMD-74098), eleven photo-crosslinking mass spectrometry hits in a PDF table, and assay results that exist only as figure panels. There is no feature/label table and no way to build one at a usable size. The structure's real value to machine learning is as a single extra entry in the PDB, which downstream structure-prediction benchmarks will pick up automatically.

effort.compute_note: Estimated, not timed: the entire deposited dataset is well under 50 MB, and embedding four protein sequences with ESM-2 on a laptop CPU takes seconds. Compute is irrelevant here; the problem is that there is nothing to compute on.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the rows in Supplementary Tables S5 and S6. I did this: 7 + 4 = 11 crosslinks. That single count kills the project in under five minutes and should always be the first thing checked on a structure paper.

verdict_reason: Fails Part A2 and A5, both verified by opening the files rather than reading the paper. This is a single-structure mechanistic study: one cryo-EM map at 3.72 Angstrom, one PDB coordinate set with four chains, and exactly 11 crosslinked peptide pairs printed in a supplementary PDF. There is no prediction target column anywhere, and no amount of effort turns 11 measurements into a training set. The remaining measurements (ATPase activity, microscopy co-localization, qPCR) appear only as figure panels, and the PRIDE mass spectrometry deposit PXD073414 is not yet public. Parts B through J were not scored, per the checklist rule to stop at the first failed killer, so the C2 existing-models audit was deliberately not run and existing_models is empty because no search was performed, not because none exist.
